version.changelog: 优化描述：面向中国电商运营，纯中文描述，突出淘宝/京东/拼多多支持

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed ecommerce review scraper and report generator, with privacy and dependency cautions but no evidence of hidden, destructive, or deceptive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires OpenClaw browser automation and a logged-in ecommerce session, which is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should scope runs to intended product pages because it collects full review text and user/date fields.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill declares unpinned pip dependencies for jieba, python-docx, and fpdf2; these are plausible for Chinese text processing and document export, but mutable package resolution should be reviewed or pinned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger examples include one broad product-feedback phrase, and the skill does not add explicit negative examples, but the surrounding instructions consistently limit operation to Taobao, JD, and Pinduoduo review analysis.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background persistence, privilege escalation, memory writes, or tool hijacking were found; the only persistence is the expected local Word/PDF report output, which may contain usernames and full comments.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser automation, review collection, sentiment-style analysis, and Word/PDF report generation all match the stated ecommerce review analysis purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using an authenticated browser session to gather ecommerce reviews and creating local reports that may include usernames, dates, and full comments. Prefer running it in a scoped browser session and pinning dependencies in a virtual environment before use.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger is a clarity issue, not evidence of unsafe behavior; the artifact otherwise describes a specific ecommerce review workflow.
[SSD-3] expected: Use of the logged-in browser session and collection of review text/user/date fields are disclosed and directly tied to ecommerce review reporting, though privacy minimization would improve the skill.
[SQP-2] expected: Local Word/PDF exports containing review details are an expected feature, but the skill should warn users more explicitly about retention and offer redaction where appropriate.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language support is consistent with the named Chinese ecommerce platforms; mixed Chinese/English examples are not a security concern.
[EA3] unexpected: The cited text is standard MIT-0 license language and does not grant runtime agency or expand the skill behavior.
[T08] expected: The unpinned Python dependencies are relevant install-risk signal, but the package names are ordinary for the stated functionality and no malicious dependency source or execution payload is present in the artifact.
